option_description: Attests the directory server rejects anonymous bind requests (no DN, no credentials), so an unauthenticated client cannot connect and enumerate the DIT.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Anonymous / unauthenticated bind directory disclosure" — the exposure fires when this attestation is false (anonymous bind accepted), permitting reconnaissance of users/groups/emails (ATT&CK T1087).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the slapd global config for the olcDisallows attribute (slapd.conf equivalent: 'disallow bind_anon').
how_to_obtain.expected_output: olcDisallows: bind_anon (secure) or attribute absent (insecure — anonymous bind permitted by default).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Empirically attempt an anonymous bind against the directory and read the result.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An error / inappropriateAuthentication (secure — anonymous bind refused) vs 'anonymous' / dn:'' returned (insecure — anonymous bind accepted).

option_description: Attests all directory operations require an authenticated identity ('require authc' / olcRequires: authc), closing the anonymous-read bypass that disabling anonymous bind alone leaves open.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Anonymous / unauthenticated bind directory disclosure" — fires when false; even with anonymous bind disabled, the server answers anonymous searches, exposing the whole tree (ATT&CK T1087).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the olcRequires attribute on the database/global config (slapd.conf: 'require authc').
how_to_obtain.expected_output: olcRequires: authc (secure) or absent (insecure).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify empirically that an anonymous search (not just bind) is refused rather than returning entries.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No entries / error without binding (secure) vs DIT entries returned to an anonymous client (insecure — directory readable without authc).

option_description: Attests a simple bind with a non-empty DN and a zero-length password (RFC 4513 §5.1.2 unauthenticated mechanism) is rejected rather than silently authenticating the named DN.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Anonymous / unauthenticated bind directory disclosure" — fires when false; a lax server authenticates the client as the named DN with an empty password, an authentication bypass (ATT&CK T1078).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the olcAllows attribute and confirm bind_anon_cred is not present (slapd.conf: 'allow bind_anon_cred').
how_to_obtain.expected_output: olcAllows does NOT contain bind_anon_cred (secure, default) vs 'olcAllows: bind_anon_cred' present (insecure).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt a simple bind with a real DN and an empty password and read the result.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Bind fails with unwillingToPerform/invalidCredentials (secure) vs authenticated as the DN with an empty password (insecure — unauthenticated bind accepted).
how_to_obtain.source: RFC 4513 §5.1.2 Unauthenticated Authentication Mechanism of Simple Bind

option_description: Whether the LDAP flow is encrypted in transit (ldaps://636 or a successfully negotiated StartTLS on 389), so the bind DN and password do not cross the wire in cleartext.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cleartext LDAP bind credential exposure / StartTLS downgrade" — fires when false; a simple bind over ldap://389 exposes the credential to network sniffing (ATT&CK T1040).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm ldaps://636 is reachable with TLS, or that StartTLS (-ZZ) succeeds on 389.
how_to_obtain.command: nmap -p 636 --script ssl-enum-ciphers HOST  # and verify 389 StartTLS via 'ldapsearch -ZZ'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ldaps:// (636) reachable with TLS, or StartTLS (-ZZ) succeeds; cleartext 389 without StartTLS = insecure.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS Managed Microsoft AD client-side LDAPS (reused corpus)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Capture the bind on the wire and confirm it is TLS, not a cleartext simple-bind DN/password.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Bind exchange is TLS-wrapped (secure) vs a readable cleartext simple-bind DN and password in the capture (insecure).

option_description: Whether the server enforces a minimum confidentiality strength so plaintext binds are refused (OpenLDAP olcSecurity ssf/minssf >= 128, or AD LDAP signing/channel-binding requirement).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cleartext LDAP bind credential exposure / StartTLS downgrade" — fires when false; without an enforced SSF the server accepts cleartext ldap://389 binds even when TLS is available (ATT&CK T1040).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read olcSecurity for an enforced minimum SSF (slapd.conf: 'security ssf=128').
how_to_obtain.expected_output: olcSecurity contains ssf>=128 (256 recommended) and/or simple_bind / update_ssf (secure) vs no olcSecurity / ssf=0 (insecure — no confidentiality enforced).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt a plaintext simple bind over port 389 and verify it is refused with confidentialityRequired.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Bind refused with confidentialityRequired over plaintext 389 (secure — TLS enforced) vs successful plaintext bind (insecure — credentials exposed).
how_to_obtain.source: AWS Managed Microsoft AD client-side LDAPS (reused corpus)

option_description: Whether StartTLS on the flow cannot be stripped or downgraded by an active attacker — TLS is mandatory (ldaps://636 or StartTLS required, bind refused without it) rather than opportunistic.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Cleartext LDAP bind credential exposure / StartTLS downgrade" — fires when false; a MITM can suppress the StartTLS upgrade and force the bind into cleartext (ATT&CK T1040).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm olcSecurity enforces an SSF so the server refuses an un-upgraded bind rather than answering it opportunistically.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: olcSecurity ssf>=128 present so a non-TLS bind is refused (secure) vs no SSF requirement, StartTLS optional/strippable (insecure).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Simulate StartTLS suppression (or point the client at plaintext 389) and confirm the bind fails rather than proceeding in cleartext; confirm whether the client uses ldaps://636 exclusively.
how_to_obtain.command: ldapwhoami -x -H ldap://HOST:389 -D 'BIND_DN' -w PW   # no -ZZ, i.e. StartTLS suppressed
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Bind refused without TLS / client only uses ldaps://636 (secure — no opportunistic fallback) vs cleartext bind proceeds (insecure — downgradeable).
how_to_obtain.source: AWS Managed Microsoft AD client-side LDAPS (reused corpus)

option_description: Minimum TLS protocol version the directory channel negotiates (olcTLSProtocolMin / observable via ssl-enum on ldaps://636 or StartTLS).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Weak/legacy TLS on the directory channel" — fires when the floor is SSLv3/TLS1.0/TLS1.1; the recommended TLS1.2/TLS1.3 do not fire. A legacy floor leaves the encrypted bind channel breakable.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read olcTLSProtocolMin to confirm the enforced floor (3.3 = TLS 1.2).
how_to_obtain.command: ldapsearch -Y EXTERNAL -H ldapi:/// -b cn=config olcTLSCipherSuite olcTLSProtocolMin
how_to_obtain.expected_output: olcTLSProtocolMin set to 3.3 (TLS 1.2) or higher (secure) vs unset/permissive allowing TLS 1.0 (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: OpenLDAP 2.5 Admin Guide — Security Considerations / Using TLS

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the protocols offered on ldaps://636 (or StartTLS on 389) and read the lowest accepted.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Lowest protocol is TLS 1.2/1.3 (secure) vs SSLv3/TLS1.0/TLS1.1 offered (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge (TLS cipher enumeration; corroborates olcTLSCipherSuite config)

option_description: Attestation that the directory channel's cipher list excludes weak/legacy suites (NULL/aNULL/eNULL, RC4, DES/3DES, EXPORT, MD5).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Weak/legacy TLS on the directory channel" — fires when false (weak ciphers still negotiable), leaving the encrypted bind channel breakable.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read olcTLSCipherSuite and confirm it excludes NULL/export/RC4/DES (e.g. a HIGH:!aNULL:!eNULL:!MD5:!RC4 form).
how_to_obtain.command: ldapsearch -Y EXTERNAL -H ldapi:/// -b cn=config olcTLSCipherSuite olcTLSProtocolMin
how_to_obtain.expected_output: olcTLSCipherSuite excludes NULL/export/RC4/DES (secure) vs unset/permissive (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: OpenLDAP 2.5 Admin Guide — Security Considerations / Using TLS

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate negotiable cipher suites on 636 and confirm no weak suites remain.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only TLS 1.2/1.3 with strong ciphers offered (secure) vs NULL/RC4/DES/3DES/EXPORT/MD5 suites listed (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge (TLS cipher enumeration; corroborates olcTLSCipherSuite config)

option_description: Attestation that all user input concatenated into LDAP search filters is escaped per RFC 4515 (* ( ) \ and NUL) or routed through a filter encoder.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "LDAP injection via unescaped search filters / DNs" — fires when false; raw input reaches the filter string, enabling uid=* / )(uid=* injection for auth bypass or full-tree disclosure (ATT&CK T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Code-review the search-filter build path: input must pass an RFC 4515 escaper / filter-encoder before concatenation.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Filters use parameterized templates or an LDAP filter encoder (LdapFilterEncode), and the four RFC 4515 chars (* ( ) \) are escaped (secure) vs raw user input concatenated into the filter (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP LDAP Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet (RFC 4515 / RFC 4514)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe the app login/search endpoints with filter-injection payloads and confirm they are treated as literals.
how_to_obtain.command: # Probe app login/search with payloads: uid=*  and  uid=*)(uid=*  and  )(uid=*))(|(uid=*
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Input rejected/escaped, login fails, no broadened result set (secure) vs authentication bypass or full-tree disclosure (insecure — filter injection).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP LDAP Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attestation that search filters are built from parameterized templates (e.g. '(&(uid={0})(objectClass=person))' with input bound separately) or an encoder API, not string concatenation.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "LDAP injection via unescaped search filters / DNs" — fires when false; concatenation of raw user input is the root cause of LDAP injection (ATT&CK T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the data-access layer: filters should use parameterized templates or an encoder API, not string concatenation.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Parameterized filter templates / encoder API (LdapFilterEncode) in use (secure) vs raw concatenation, e.g. `+`-style filter assembly (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP LDAP Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet (RFC 4515 / RFC 4514)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the application source for string-concatenated filter assembly as a negative signal.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No concatenated filter assembly found; matches resolve to template/encoder calls (secure) vs raw `+`-concatenated filter strings (insecure).

option_description: Attestation that user input placed into Distinguished Names is escaped per the broader RFC 4514 metacharacter set (or allow-listed).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "LDAP injection via unescaped search filters / DNs" — fires when false; an attacker injects DN metachars to alter the target DN of a bind or modify operation (ATT&CK T1190).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Code-review DN composition from user input: confirm RFC 4514 escaping (or strict allow-listing) via a DN encoder.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: DNs built with an RFC 4514 encoder (LdapDistinguishedNameEncode) or allow-listed (secure) vs raw input concatenated into the DN (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP LDAP Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet (RFC 4515 / RFC 4514)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Test with DN injection characters and verify the target DN is not altered.
how_to_obtain.command: # Probe with DN metachars in the username field: ,  +  =  \  #
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Metachars escaped, target DN unchanged (secure) vs the bind/modify DN is altered (insecure — DN injection).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP LDAP Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attests the directory's olcAccess/access ACLs scope read to only the principals that require it and every chain terminates in 'by * none' — no catch-all 'access to * by * read'.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Over-permissive directory ACL / userPassword hash disclosure" — fires when false; a catch-all read ACL exposes the whole DIT to anonymous/low-privilege clients for reconnaissance (ATT&CK T1087).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the olcAccess rules and confirm each chain ends 'by * none' with no catch-all read clause.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ACLs scope read to 'users'/specific DNs and end 'by * none' (secure) vs a rule granting 'by * read' or 'by anonymous read' on '*' (insecure — whole-DIT disclosure).

how_to_obtain.instruction: As an anonymous/low-priv client, attempt to read entries and sensitive/operational attributes across the tree.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Anonymous/low-priv client cannot read the tree or sensitive attrs (secure) vs entries with operational/sensitive attributes returned (insecure — over-broad ACL).

option_description: Attests a dedicated ACL gates userPassword (and other secrets) to 'by self =xw by anonymous auth by * none', preceding the generic read rule.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Over-permissive directory ACL / userPassword hash disclosure" — fires when false; userPassword falls through to a generic read clause and hashes are readable for offline cracking (ATT&CK T1003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a dedicated userPassword ACL precedes any generic read rule.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A specific 'access to attrs=userPassword by self =xw by anonymous auth by * none' rule precedes the generic read rule (secure) vs no such rule (insecure — userPassword falls through to read).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt to read userPassword as an anonymous/low-priv (non-self) client.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: userPassword empty/no-access for non-self readers (secure) vs the hash returned (insecure — password disclosure).

option_description: Attests anonymous clients cannot read the full directory tree — anonymous read of the DIT is denied (no anonymous 'by * read' on '*').
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Over-permissive directory ACL / userPassword hash disclosure" — fires when false; an anonymous client can enumerate the entire tree, the precondition turning an over-broad ACL into full-DIT disclosure (ATT&CK T1087).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run an anonymous full-subtree search and confirm it cannot enumerate the whole DIT.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No entries / refused for the anonymous client (secure) vs the full tree enumerated (insecure — anonymous 'by * read' on '*').

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read olcAccess and confirm no rule grants anonymous read on '*'.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No 'by anonymous read' / 'by * read' on '*' (secure) vs such a clause present (insecure).

option_description: Attestation that the service bind-DN password is stored in plaintext in application config or environment files (a literal bindpw/ldap.password value rather than a runtime reference).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Privileged bind-DN credential in app config" — fires when true; a plaintext bind credential is a high-value secret whose leak grants the app's directory privileges (ATT&CK T1552.001 Credentials In Files).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Audit the application config/env directory for a literal bind-DN password.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No plaintext bind password (only a runtime secret reference) = secure (false); a literal bind-DN password appearing in config/env = insecure (true, fires).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP LDAP Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet (complementary: least-privilege bind account)

option_description: Attestation that the bind-DN credential is resolved at runtime from a secret manager (or a SASL EXTERNAL/GSSAPI/certificate bind is used) rather than held as a static value in app config.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Privileged bind-DN credential in app config" — fires when false; a non-externalized in-config bind credential is the leakable secret behind this dataFlow's directory access (ATT&CK T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the bind credential is fetched at runtime from a secret store (or a SASL/cert bind is used), and that config holds only a reference/path.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Credential resolved from a secret store at runtime / SASL EXTERNAL or GSSAPI bind; config holds only a reference (secure) vs static password embedded in config (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP LDAP Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet (complementary: least-privilege bind account)

option_description: Attestation that the service bind account has a least-privilege, read-only ACL scoped to only the entries/attributes the app needs, rather than a broad or directory-admin-equivalent grant.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Privileged bind-DN credential in app config" — fires when false; an over-privileged bind account widens the blast radius of a leaked credential to the whole DIT, often with write (ATT&CK T1552).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the olcAccess rules referencing the service bind DN and confirm they grant only minimal read and terminate in 'by * none'.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Bind DN's ACLs grant only the minimal read it needs and end 'by * none' (secure) vs directory-admin or write-equivalent access (insecure).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Bind as the service account and attempt a write/modify beyond its intended scope to confirm it is denied.
how_to_obtain.command: ldapmodify -x -H ldap://HOST -D 'BIND_DN' -w PW   # attempt a modify outside the app's scope
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Out-of-scope write denied with insufficientAccessRights (secure — read-only least-privilege) vs the modify succeeds (insecure — over-privileged bind).

option_description: Storage scheme used for the userPassword attribute, set by slapd olcPasswordHash (or the FreeIPA/AD equivalent).
security_impact: Triggers "Weak password-hash storage scheme" — fires when the scheme is one of the weak values (sha, crypt, cleartext); on disclosure the hash is trivially recovered (ATT&CK T1003). Salted strong schemes (argon2/bcrypt/ssha) do not fire.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read olcPasswordHash (slapd) or the FreeIPA/AD equivalent.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: olcPasswordHash: {SSHA} (or argon2/bcrypt module) (secure) vs {CLEARTEXT} / unsalted (insecure).
how_to_obtain.source: OpenLDAP 2.5 Admin Guide — Security Considerations (password storage)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Where readable to an admin, sample a stored userPassword value and read its {SCHEME} prefix.
how_to_obtain.command: # Where readable to admin: inspect a userPassword value prefix
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Value begins with {SSHA}/{ARGON2}/{BCRYPT} (secure) vs plaintext or {CRYPT} weak hash (insecure).

option_description: Attests the directory bind endpoint enforces an account-lockout policy (OpenLDAP ppolicy overlay with pwdLockout: TRUE and bounded pwdMaxFailure/pwdLockoutDuration; equivalent on AD/FreeIPA).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Missing lockout / unbounded search (brute-force & resource exhaustion)" — fires when false; the bind endpoint accepts unlimited attempts, exposing every account to brute-force/password-spray (ATT&CK T1110).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the ppolicy overlay is loaded and read pwdLockout/pwdMaxFailure/pwdLockoutDuration on the policy entry.
how_to_obtain.command: ldapsearch -Y EXTERNAL -H ldapi:/// -b cn=config '(olcOverlay=ppolicy)' && ldapsearch -x -D 'BIND_DN' -W -b 'POLICY_DN' pwdLockout pwdMaxFailure pwdLockoutDuration
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ppolicy overlay present; pwdLockout: TRUE, pwdMaxFailure small (e.g. 5), pwdLockoutDuration set (secure) vs overlay absent or pwdLockout FALSE (insecure).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Empirically attempt repeated bad binds against a test account and confirm it locks.
how_to_obtain.command: for i in $(seq 1 10); do ldapwhoami -x -H ldap://HOST -D 'cn=testuser,BASE_DN' -w wrongpw; done
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Account locks after the bounded failure count (secure) vs unlimited attempts accepted (insecure).

option_description: Attests directory searches are bounded by enforced size and time limits (olcSizeLimit/olcTimeLimit, bounded paged-result size.prtotal, tighter per-initiator olcLimits for anonymous/unprivileged clients).
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Missing lockout / unbounded search (brute-force & resource exhaustion)" — fires when false; a single client can run unbounded searches to exhaust resources or mass-exfiltrate the DIT (ATT&CK T1499).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read olcSizeLimit/olcTimeLimit/olcLimits and confirm bounded values plus tighter limits for untrusted initiators.
how_to_obtain.command: ldapsearch -Y EXTERNAL -H ldapi:/// -b cn=config olcSizeLimit olcTimeLimit olcLimits
how_to_obtain.expected_output: olcSizeLimit bounded (default 500) and olcTimeLimit bounded (default 3600); olcLimits restrict anonymous/unprivileged initiators; size.prtotal not 'unlimited' for untrusted clients (secure) vs 'unlimited' values (insecure).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run a broad search and verify it is capped rather than returning the whole DIT.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Result capped with sizeLimitExceeded / timeLimitExceeded (secure) vs the whole DIT returned in one query (insecure — unbounded search).
